Diego to run 1-hour latency benchmark on their EU test shard and share results by 2026-05-05
Customer to confirm internal sign-off timeline and any additional compliance docs needed by 2026-05-10

header:
Date: 2026-04-29 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins | Recording: Enabled | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE); Diego Ramos (Redwood SE); Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM); Lena Morris (Oxley VP AI); Tomislav Novak (Oxley CTO); Rina Sato (Cloud Eng); Marcus Li (Procurement)
summary: Renewal discussion focused on adding a Dedicated capacity uplift for Oxleyâ€™s EU workloads and transitioning a portion of traffic to an on-prem (air-gapped-ish) footprint. Key blockers: KMS integration, SOC2 attestation timing, and network peering constraints. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide revised TCO and benchmark results; customer to provide network topology and procurement timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, welcome. Thanks for carving out time, we'll just do a quick recap then dig into the EU on-prem transition and the renewal sizing.
[00:25] Lena: Thanks, Samira. Quick note - Marcus is here for procurement questions later, but the core technicals are with me and Rina.
[00:32] Diego: Great. I have the previous benchmark summary up, and Priya will jump in on renewals cadence.
[00:45] Tomislav: Just so you know, our ops team flagged two things: KMS must be customer-managed, and we need audit logs forwarded into our SIEM.
[01:05] Samira: Totally understood, and that's in our private plan - KMS/HSM integrations are supported, and we do have streaming audit logs. We'll send you the SOC and audit pack after.
[01:28] Rina: Small clarification - when you say streaming audit logs, is that syslog over TCP or direct S3 export? Which one maps to our SIEM?
[01:45] Diego: Right now we support S3 export with event metadata and a syslog bridge. There was a recent enhancement to push events to a Kinesis-like endpoint but I'll caveat that with what we've got in EU on-prem.
[02:10] Lena: Another big one is latency — our customer-facing flows are very latency sensitive. We want to know the delta between Dedicated in Redwood's EU region vs our on-prem node.
[02:34] Samira: We expected that. Diego, can you walk through the predicted tail latencies and batching tradeoffs?
[02:40] Diego: Yep. So, rough ballpark: hosting in our EU region with Dedicated typically gives you 50-80ms p95 for typical 256-token generation if you size as discussed. On-prem depends on your NICs and NVLINK configs; we saw 40-60ms p95 on colocated racks with direct NVLink, but the variance increases if your app is behind NAT or slow peering. Also batching settings change effective latency - bigger batches reduce cost but add queuing.
[03:22] Tomislav: Are those numbers with KV cache warm? We have long-running chat sessions so warm cache behavior matters.
[03:35] Diego: Good call, the numbers I mentioned assume warm KV cache for the session. Cold starts add 20-40ms depending on sequence length. Also note our continuous batching can stitch short requests, so for spiky traffic it helps.
[04:00] Marcus: On procurement, timeline wise we need final pricing and contract language by early May to route for end-of-quarter approvals.
[04:15] Samira: We'll prioritize that. Priya, can you speak to the renewal cadence and what we'll provide?
[04:22] Priya: Sure — we can get a revised TCO and commitment options (monthly vs annual) to Marcus by 2026-05-03. We'll include Dedicated uplift scenarios and burst policies.
[04:40] Lena: Another practical thing — can you confirm data residency? Some of our EU customers require data never leaves EU.
[04:50] Samira: For Dedicated in our EU region we store tokens and logs in-region. For Private on-prem it stays on your network. We'll include explicit data-flow diagrams.
[05:05] Tomislav: For the on-prem pilot, we expect to run a single test node in our Frankfurt DC. We need the installer and a checklist. Is there an air-gap option?
[05:20] Diego: Yes, we have an on-prem package that supports VPC-only and air-gapped install with an offline license. The offline install requires a slightly different package for model weights and a secure handoff for kernels. I'll attach the runbook link.
[05:45] Rina: Any differences in model variants when on-prem compared to hosted? We use redwood-7b-quant for most of the preproc.
[05:55] Diego: On-prem supports the same model catalog; however, depending on GPU/quant settings you'll see different throughput. Our recommendation is to pin a quant profile - e.g., int4-optimized kernel - for consistent latency. For strict compliance we might provision a compatible variant but same architecture.
[06:20] Lena: What about key rotation? We need to ensure KMS rotation cadence matches our policies.
[06:30] Samira: We support customer KMS with automatic rotation hooks; rotation can be pushed via KMS endpoint or manual rotation windows. We'll include a KMS integration spec in the security pack.
[06:48] Tomislav: Is Redwood able to run A/B traffic split during the rollout? We want to start 10% on-hosted, 90% on-prem then ramp.
[07:00] Diego: Yes, routing policies support percentage-based splits and fallbacks. If the on-prem node becomes unavailable, traffic can failover to Dedicated or hosted variants with configurable thresholds.
[07:30] Marcus: Any price delta for the split/fallback traffic? Our finance team wants to know worst-case spend.
[07:40] Samira: We'll model both best- and worst-case in the TCO. Typically, failover to hosted will incur on-demand rates; we can also reserve burst capacity to cap costs.
[08:00] Rina: Networking — we need specifics on ports and CIDR ranges for peering. Who provides those?
[08:10] Diego: We'll provide a network appendix with ports, CIDRs, and a validation checklist. For on-prem peering we recommend a private peering circuit where possible.
[08:40] Lena: Security review — SOC2 Type II is in your pack? We need the report and recent penetration test summary.
[08:50] Priya: Yes, SOC2 type II report is included in our security pack and we have a pen test summary. I will mark that as high priority to share post-call.
[09:10] Tomislav: A small note on model updates: our legal wants guarantees that model weights aren't changed mid-contract in a way that materially changes outputs. Do you have a model-change policy?
[09:30] Samira: We do. Model versioning and rollout windows are part of Redwood Console. We can pin model versions for Dedicated/Private and schedule controlled rollouts — and alert when a model family update is proposed.
[09:55] Lena: Perfect. Can we also get an eval harness to run our in-house prompts against the candidate models?
[10:05] Diego: Absolutely. We can give you access to a sandbox with the eval runner and your prompt set to track regressions and quality.
[10:30] Marcus: Procurement question — do you accept procurement redlines or do we need to use your standard contract?
[10:40] Samira: We can accept up to a limited set of redlines; large deviations will go to legal review. We'll flag any material ones early.
[11:00] Rina: On the technical onboarding timeline — how long to stand up the on-prem node?
[11:08] Diego: If hardware is ready and networking is arranged, we estimate 2-3 weeks for initial install and smoke tests. More if HSM/KMS provisioning is complex.
[11:30] Lena: For the benchmark, can you include a p99 estimate? We need worst-case numbers for SLA.
[11:40] Diego: Yes, we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and tail distributions. I'll run an explicit long tail test.
[12:05] Tomislav: Any gotchas from other customers doing similar EU on-prem transitions?
[12:15] Samira: Common gotchas: underprovisioned NICs causing high tail, misconfigured KMS endpoints adding latency, and forgetting to pin quant kernels leading to drift in throughput.
[12:40] Lena: On monitoring — does the console give token-level cost and per-route dashboards?
[12:52] Priya: Yes, the Console gives token-level breakdown, per-model latency and cost, and traces for slow requests. We can export dashboards to Grafana too.
[13:15] Marcus: Do you offer any billing hold or credits for migration regressions?
[13:25] Samira: We typically negotiate a short migration credit for first-month anomalies as part of the contract. We'll propose something in the renewal offer.
[13:50] Rina: Another nit — how do you handle data retention for logs? We need 7 years for audit artifacts in some jurisdictions.
[14:05] Priya: By default we retain logs for 90 days on hosted; enterprise packages can extend retention or stream to your storage for long-term archival. We'll include options.
[14:30] Tomislav: Okay, let's walk through the timeline concretely. We need final price by 2026-05-03, procurement approvals by 2026-05-15, and a pilot start the week of 2026-05-25. Is that realistic?
[14:48] Samira: Yes that's realistic. We'll aim to hit that.
[15:00] Diego: I'll schedule the benchmark runs for this week and send the results early next week.
[15:20] Lena: One more technical — does Redwood support per-customer RBAC and SSO via SAML?
[15:30] Priya: Yes, SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported. We'll include an example assertion mapping.
[15:50] Marcus: Quick question on encryption in flight — TLS version and mutual TLS support?
[15:58] Diego: TLS 1.2+ supported and mTLS is available for private peering.
[16:15] Rina: About the on-prem installer: do you need root access? Our security team will likely only grant sudo to a narrow set.
[16:25] Diego: Installer requires sudo for kernel modules and GPU drivers; we have a checklist to run under an ops account. For air-gapped installs we also provide a pre-built VM image.
[16:50] Lena: Great. Any open items we haven't covered?
[17:00] Samira: We didn't confirm SLOs exactly. For Dedicated we'll propose a 99.9% availability SLA and latency SLO language — I'll include the wording.
[17:20] Marcus: Okay. If we can get pricing and the SOC2 pack this week, procurement will be happy.
[17:30] Priya: I'll send the security pack within 24 hours.
[17:45] Tomislav: Diego, can you confirm the specific ports and a sample test plan for peering?
[17:52] Diego: Yes, I'll attach a network appendix and a test script to validate MTU and latency.
[18:10] Samira: Recap: Redwood to send TCO + Dedicated/Hosted scenarios, security pack, network appendix, and benchmark plan. Oxley to share peering topology and procurement timeline. Next sync tentatively 2026-05-07.
[18:35] Lena: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[18:45] Marcus: Thanks.
[18:50] Samira: Thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and action items.
[19:00] -- End of recording --

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache) and some proper nouns may be slightly off. Links referenced: security pack (link: https://redwood.example/security-pack/oxley-2026), TCO spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example/tco/oxley-2026), on-prem runbook (link: https://redwood.example/onprem/runbook).
